Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:10:1.hebrew: לנקוטינהו לשמעתתיה - נתקבצו לבהמ"ד, ואמרו: כל ששמע שמועה חדשה מפיו, יאמרנה באזני חביריו, כדי לצרפם שלא ישתכחו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:10:1.english: To collect his statements - They gathered in the study hall and said: Whoever heard a new teaching from his mouth, let him recite it in the hearing of his colleagues, in order to combine them so that they will not be forgotten.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:11:1.hebrew: קונין - בחליפין, "שלף איש נעלו" (רות ד׳:ז׳):
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:11:1.english: One can acquire - Through [symbolic] exchange, [as in the verse:] "A man drew off his shoe" (Ruth 4:7).

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:12:1.hebrew: הדר יתבי וקאמרי - בשמעתיה דר' אסי: הא דאמר רב יהודה כו', א"ר אסי עלה: קשים לעולם דיינים המורים הוראה בעריות ואינם בקיאין, יותר מדור המבול:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:12:1.english: They then sat and said - [This was] among the teachings of Rabbi Asi: [Regarding] that which Rav Yehuda said, etc., Rabbi Asi said about it: Judges who issue rulings in [matters of] forbidden relations and are not expert [in them] are more harmful to the world than the generation of the Flood.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:12:2.hebrew: פרצו - כמו וכן יפרוץ (שמות א), מולדין בנין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:12:2.english: They break all bounds - Like “and so they spread abroad” (Exodus 1:12), [meaning] they beget children.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:13:1.hebrew: מאי משמע - מהכא קשים לעולם, דקאי ״על כן תאבל״ אאשת איש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:13:1.english: From where is it inferred - [How is it inferred] from here [that they are] worse for the world, [and] that "Therefore [the land] mourns" refers to a married woman?

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:13:2.hebrew: כדמתרגם רב יוסף - דהוה בקי בתרגום נביאים שתרגם יונתן בן עוזיאל, דהאי "פרצו דמים בדמים נגעו" באשת איש קאי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:13:2.english: As Rav Yosef translated - For he was expert in the translation of the Prophets that Yonatan ben Uzziel translated, [which shows] that this [phrase], “they break all bounds, [and] blood touches blood,” refers to a married woman.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:15:1.hebrew: כי מפני אלה אבלה הארץ - בעלמא כתיב, מיהא שמעינן מינה דאכל חדא קאמר ״על כן תאבל״, דהא אלה חדא מהנך דקרא קמא היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:15:1.english: For because of swearing the land mourns - [This verse] is written elsewhere; nevertheless, we learn from it that [Scripture] says "Therefore the land mourns" regarding each individual one, for swearing is one of those [sins] in the first verse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:1:1.english: If she said "No," it would also be a betrothal - [This is said] in astonishment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:1:2.hebrew: דשתקה מישתקה - ולא רצתה דקאמר, ה"ק: לא אמרה רוצה אני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:1:2.english: That she remained silent - And [as for] that which it says, "She did not want" — this is what it is saying: She did not say, "I want."

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:1:3.english: It is nothing - For this [fact] that she remained silent is because she does not care.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:2:1.english: Is it comparable? - [Is] the silence here [comparable] to the silence there?

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:2:2.hebrew: התם - גבי כנסי בפקדון, מעיקרא בתורה שמירה קבילתיה. כי הדר אמר התקדשי לי בו, סברה: אי שדינא ליה כו'. הילכך, לא שדתינהו, והאי דלא מחאי — משום דלא איכפת לה. אבל גבי ציפתא, מעיקרא בתורת קידושין קבלתיה. ונהי דציפתא לית בה שוה פרוטה, כי הדר ואמר תקדוש בזוזי דאית בה, אי לא ניחא לה — תשדינהו, דהא לא נתחייבה בשמירתה. ומדלא שדתינהו, ש"מ נתרצית בקידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:2:2.english: There - Regarding [the case of] "Take [this] as a deposit," she initially accepted it under [the terms of] safekeeping. When he subsequently said, "Be betrothed to me with it," she reasoned: "If I throw it, etc." Therefore, she did not throw them [away]; and the fact that she did not protest was because it did not matter to her. But regarding the mat, she initially accepted it under [the terms of] betrothal; and even though the mat does not have the value of a perutah, when he subsequently said, "Let her be betrothed with the coins that are in it," if she was not amenable, let her throw them [away]! For she had not become obligated in its safekeeping; and since she did not throw them [away], learn from it that she consented to the betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:3:1.hebrew: דינא גמירי - וידעה, כיון דלא קבלה נטירותא עלה, אי שדיא להו, לא תחייב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:3:1.english: [Are] learned in the law - And she knows that since she did not accept safeguarding upon herself, if she throws them, she will not be liable.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:3:2.english: We did not hear [it] - Neither did he say [it] to us, nor did another in his name.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:3:3.english: Be concerned about it - And require her [to receive] a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:5:1.english: Robbery - Where he did not give money.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:5:2.hebrew: חמסן - דיהיב דמי, אבל לא נתרצו בעלים מעולם למכור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:5:2.english: An extortionist - [One] who gives money, but the owner never consented to sell.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:5:3.hebrew: בדשדיך - שדבר בה קודם לכן ונתרצית להתקדש לו, דהתם, כי שתקה, משום דניחא לה הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:5:3.english: Where he arranged - That he spoke with her beforehand and she agreed to be betrothed to him; for there, when she was silent, it was because it was pleasing to her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:7:1.hebrew: נימא מקודשת סתם - ולא איצטריך לפלוגי ולמימר דכי אמרה לא, אינה מקודשת, שאף הקטנים יודעים בו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:7:1.english: Let it say "she is betrothed" without specification - And it would not have been necessary to distinguish and say that when she said "no", she is not betrothed, for even children know this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:7:2.hebrew: כי התם - כדתנא בההיא דלעיל: ״בשעת מתן מעות מקודשת״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:7:2.english: As there - As was taught in that [baraita] above: “At the time the money was given, she is betrothed.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:8:1.hebrew: לא רצתה דאישתיקה - וקבילתיה, ואפ"ה אינה מקודשת, דדידה שקלה. ולאחר מתן מעות, אפילו רצתה — דאמרה אין — לא מקדשה, דמעיקרא קבלתיה בחובה, וכי הדר אמרה אין, לא קיהיב לה מידי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:8:1.english: “She did not want,” that she remained silent - And she accepted it, and even so she is not betrothed, for she took what was hers. And after the giving of the money, even if she wanted — [meaning] that she said “yes” — she is not betrothed, because initially she accepted it toward her debt, and when she subsequently says “yes”, he is not giving her anything.

Rashi on Kiddushin 13a:9:1.english: And but that is difficult, etc. - This is the conclusion of [the inquiry,] “From where do you say [it]?”

Tosafot on Kiddushin 13a:10:1.hebrew: כשם שאין האשה נקנית בפחות משוה פרוטה כך אין הקרקע נקנית כו' - תימה: דה"ל למידק איפכא, דהא קניני אשה לא ידעינן אלא משדה. ושמא י"ל, דלית ליה ג"ש דקיחה קיחה, אלא נפקא ליה מ"ויצאה חנם". א"נ י"ל, דאורחיה דגמ' למינקט הפשוט תחילה, כדאי' בנדרים (דף כה:): "כשם שנדרי שגגות מותרות כך שבועות שגגות מותרות" — ואע"ג דנדר לא ידעינן אלא משבועות, דכתיב: "האדם בשבועה" — פרט לאנוס (שבועות דף כו:):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 13a:10:1.english: "Just as a woman cannot be acquired with less than the value of a perutah, so too land cannot be acquired, etc." - This is puzzling, for it should have inferred the reverse, since we know the acquisition of a woman only from [the acquisition of a] field! And perhaps one can say that he does not hold of the gezerah shavah of kikha [and] kikha, but rather derives it from: "And she shall go out free" [Exodus 21:11]. Alternatively, one can say that it is the way of the Gemara to state that which is straightforward first, as it is [taught] in Nedarim (25b): "Just as vows [made in] error are permitted, so too oaths [made in] error are permitted" — even though [the rule for] a vow we know only from oaths, as it is written: "a person in an oath" [Leviticus 5:4] — excluding one [acting] under duress (Shevuot 26a).
